metadata.description: All active home stadiums used by National Football League teams in the United States.
metadata.author: Journey

journey.name: U.S. NFL Football Stadiums
journey.description: Visit the 30 active stadiums used by all 32 NFL teams, from historic venues such as Lambeau Field and Soldier Field to modern landmarks including SoFi Stadium, Allegiant Stadium, and Buffalo's new Highmark Stadium.

items.name: Acrisure Stadium
items.description: Home of the Pittsburgh Steelers, this open-air stadium sits along Pittsburgh's North Shore near the meeting of the Allegheny, Monongahela, and Ohio rivers.

items.name: Allegiant Stadium
items.description: Home of the Las Vegas Raiders, this enclosed stadium near the Las Vegas Strip features a retractable natural-grass playing field.

items.name: AT&T Stadium
items.description: Home of the Dallas Cowboys, this retractable-roof stadium in Arlington is known for its enormous center-hung video board and major-event atmosphere.

items.name: Bank of America Stadium
items.description: Home of the Carolina Panthers, this open-air stadium stands in uptown Charlotte and also hosts major soccer and entertainment events.

items.name: Caesars Superdome
items.description: Home of the New Orleans Saints, this iconic domed stadium has anchored the city's sports and entertainment district for decades.

items.name: Empower Field at Mile High
items.description: Home of the Denver Broncos, this open-air stadium carries forward Denver's Mile High football tradition near downtown and the Rocky Mountain Front Range.

items.name: EverBank Stadium
items.description: Home of the Jacksonville Jaguars, this open-air riverfront stadium is known for warm-weather football and distinctive poolside viewing areas.

items.name: Ford Field
items.description: Home of the Detroit Lions, this downtown indoor stadium incorporates a historic warehouse facade and sits beside Comerica Park.

items.name: GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium
items.description: Home of the Kansas City Chiefs, this open-air stadium is celebrated for its passionate tailgating culture and famously loud game-day environment.

items.name: Gillette Stadium
items.description: Home of the New England Patriots, this open-air stadium anchors the Patriot Place entertainment complex in Foxborough.

items.name: Hard Rock Stadium
items.description: Home of the Miami Dolphins, this canopy-covered stadium in Miami Gardens hosts football, international soccer, tennis, concerts, and other major events.

items.name: Highmark Stadium
items.description: Home of the Buffalo Bills beginning with the 2026 season, this football-first open-air stadium continues the franchise's tradition in Orchard Park.

items.name: Huntington Bank Field
items.description: Home of the Cleveland Browns, this open-air stadium occupies a prominent Lake Erie waterfront site in downtown Cleveland.

items.name: Lambeau Field
items.description: Home of the Green Bay Packers, this historic outdoor stadium is one of professional football's most recognizable and tradition-rich venues.

items.name: Levi's Stadium
items.description: Home of the San Francisco 49ers, this open-air stadium in Santa Clara combines modern technology with views toward the surrounding Silicon Valley.

items.name: Lincoln Financial Field
items.description: Home of the Philadelphia Eagles, this open-air stadium is a centerpiece of the South Philadelphia Sports Complex and one of the league's most energetic venues.

items.name: Lucas Oil Stadium
items.description: Home of the Indianapolis Colts, this downtown stadium features a retractable roof, a large operable window, and convenient access to the convention district.

items.name: Lumen Field
items.description: Home of the Seattle Seahawks, this downtown open-air stadium is designed to amplify crowd noise and offers views toward Seattle's skyline and waterfront.

items.name: M&T Bank Stadium
items.description: Home of the Baltimore Ravens, this open-air stadium stands near Baltimore's Inner Harbor and Camden Yards.

items.name: Mercedes-Benz Stadium
items.description: Home of the Atlanta Falcons, this downtown stadium is recognized for its retractable pinwheel roof and circular halo video board.

items.name: MetLife Stadium
items.description: Shared by the New York Giants and New York Jets, this open-air stadium anchors the Meadowlands Sports Complex in East Rutherford.

items.name: Nissan Stadium
items.description: Home of the Tennessee Titans through the 2026 season, this open-air stadium sits beside the Cumberland River across from downtown Nashville.

items.name: Northwest Stadium
items.description: Home of the Washington Commanders, this open-air stadium is located in Landover, Maryland, just east of Washington, D.C.

items.name: NRG Stadium
items.description: Home of the Houston Texans, this retractable-roof stadium is part of the NRG Park complex and hosts major sporting and entertainment events.

items.name: Paycor Stadium
items.description: Home of the Cincinnati Bengals, this open-air stadium overlooks the Ohio River along downtown Cincinnati's riverfront.

items.name: Raymond James Stadium
items.description: Home of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, this open-air stadium is famous for its large pirate ship and lively end-zone atmosphere.

items.name: SoFi Stadium
items.description: Shared by the Los Angeles Rams and Los Angeles Chargers, this landmark stadium in Inglewood sits beneath a sweeping translucent canopy.

items.name: Soldier Field
items.description: Home of the Chicago Bears, this historic lakefront stadium blends its original classical colonnades with a modern seating bowl.

items.name: State Farm Stadium
items.description: Home of the Arizona Cardinals, this retractable-roof stadium in Glendale also features a roll-out natural-grass playing field.

items.name: U.S. Bank Stadium
items.description: Home of the Minnesota Vikings, this enclosed downtown stadium features a transparent roof and dramatic glass entrance doors.
